units.note: Greek ends mid-sentence (genitives governed by a lost verb/noun); English dash at end and start of ch.6 marks this adequately. 'oude kata mikron' is slightly ambiguous in isolation but context (house of Brachylles flourishing) supports the English.

findings.quote: The man who contributed most to this state of things was Opheltas, who was forever devising
findings.problem: Greek has a lacuna: 'πλεῖστα δὲ συνεβάλετο πρὸς τὴν τοιαύτην *  ** Ὀφέλτας, αἰεί τι προσεπινοῶν' - text is missing after 'τοιαύτην' (the noun, and the subject's start) and before Ὀφέλτας. The English reads on as if whole and supplies a complete subject/predicate. The nominative Ὀφέλτας may be the subject or in apposition to a lost name; it is not certain Opheltas is the one who 'contributed most'.
findings.proposed_fix: Most contributed to such a [gap in the Greek] ... Opheltas, who was forever devising

units.note: Lacuna marked in Greek with * and ** at 'πρὸς τὴν τοιαύτην *' / '** Ὀφέλτας'. Rest of chapter checked clean.
Latin fragment 'Nec praeter quingentos' is a truncated sentence; English 'or so' is a slight softening but not a sense error.
